## Exercises (sample)

1. The client can hang / get an empty incomplete response — always continue the chain **or** write status + body yourself.
2. **Before** (and their after-code runs on the way back).
3. Give A a lower `@Order` (or lower `FilterRegistrationBean` order) so it wraps B.
4. Easy to forget endpoints; duplicated code; inconsistent status/messages.
5. Method + URI, status code, duration (and carefully chosen headers).

## Self-check

1. `jakarta.servlet.Filter` (or `javax.servlet.Filter` on older stacks).
2. **False.** Filters are servlet API; Interceptors are Spring MVC (next lecture).
3. `@Order(1)` runs earlier on the way in than `@Order(10)`.
4. **After** `chain.doFilter`, so you measure the full downstream work.
